content.comment_body: Hello everyone! I'm facing a challenge and hope someone here can assist. I need to control the speed of a motor using a [product_name] module together with a [product_name] frequency converter. I have two push buttons: one for increasing speed and one for decreasing it, connected to a 0-10V analog output. The motor's maximum speed should be around 50Hz. My issue is figuring out how to change the speed in steps of 5%, and I couldn't find a solution elsewhere. Can anyone help? Thanks! Best regards, [user_name]
Hello. Check if the attached file assists with your problem.
Hi, you're almost there—just update V2 off block B003 to 50. The analog value in [product_name] is expressed from 0 to 1000. Regards,

Thanks for the fast reply! I couldn’t open the file; [product_name] software said it couldn’t load the data. Could this be because I’m using an older version (V6.1.5)? Regards, [user_name] [EDIT] It worked now! I was able to open it. Thank you, this solves my issue perfectly!

analysis.insight_summary: Participants shared how to incrementally change an analog output using [product_name] hardware and software in a motor control project. The main concern was adjusting the output by 5% increments and understanding value representation across software versions. The discussion resolved with satisfaction after a file exchange and clarification about value scaling.
analysis.user_expectations: Users are looking for straightforward ways to apply percentage-based changes to analog outputs and want reliable compatibility between program files across different [product_name] software versions.
